summary: Third runner invocation for step M1-S03, a rebuild after the operator's dry-run validation 3 compiled run 2's package and returned eleven errors. The step had already been reset tested -> failed -> pending -> running by the operator, so this agent issued no claim of its own and invoked apex-builder inline against the org's verbatim findings. Two roots were fixed in three call sites across three files and every other artefact is byte-identical to run 2: URL.getSalesforceBaseUrl -> URL.getOrgDomainUrl in two classes, and two SOQL filters on a Long Text Area replaced by select-then-pick helpers in one test. check-outputs is ok on all 20 declared paths, the three declared checkers exit 0 with zero findings, and both envelopes validate, so the step was set built. Nothing was deployed, no sf command or mock_deploy.py was run, no gate was written, and nothing outside artefacts/M1-S03/ and envelopes/M1-S03/ was touched. The rebuild leaves the milestone above this step stale: M1-S03 must be re-tested and re-documented, and the M1 verification re-run.
confidence_rationale: MEDIUM per this agent's Step 9 table: five undeclared artefacts sit under artefacts/M1-S03/, which is the table's MEDIUM row, unchanged from run 2. Everything else is the HIGH row - check-outputs exited 0, both envelopes validate, every required input resolved from plan.json, and no file landed outside the step's artefact directory. The score deliberately does not read as reassurance: run 2 carried the same MEDIUM and the org rejected it, and run 3 has not been compiled by anything.

process_observations.observation: The org's findings arrived as verbatim messages against named components rather than as a summary, so the rebuild could be scoped to two roots and nine cascades without re-deriving the triage - and the rebuild touched three call sites rather than the eight components the error list named.

The documented-to-running rebuild path standards/build-orchestration.md section 4 describes did what it exists for: the step dropped back, the failure and both fixes are recorded in runs[] and in the step's own deploy-order.md section 0, and no plan field was hand-edited to get there.

This step reached built once, passed step-tester's five acceptance tests, and was then rejected eleven times by the first org that compiled it - so for this step the whole offline gate set, three checkers and two always-on checks, carried no signal about deployability at all.

Both faults were facts about metadata this build itself owns - the apiVersion in the step's own meta XML, and a field type M1-S01 declared - and no offline artefact in this repo joins Apex to either, which is why a corpus grep passed a method removed nine versions earlier and no checker read a field definition another step wrote.

The milestone above this step is now stale - M1 was verified on a package the org has since rejected - and re-running the tester and the doc keeper on M1-S03 is necessary but not sufficient: /verify-milestone has to run again before the M1 gate means anything.

section_3_1_support_gaps: The loop has no offline check that joins emitted Apex to the apiVersion its own meta XML declares. apex-builder's Gate C check 2 greps the corpus for an identifier, which passed a method removed after 58.0 into a 67.0 class from three skills that spell it without naming a ceiling. A version-aware attestation - the skill naming the API range an idiom is legal in, and the check reading it - is the fix; a grep is not.

No declared checker reads the field definitions another step wrote, so Apex querying a custom field cannot be validated against that field's type offline. A WHERE clause on a LongTextArea is statically decidable from artefacts/M1-S01 plus the step's own SOQL, and nothing in the library decides it. This is the cross-referential-checker problem section 5 already names for four checkers, in a shape the list does not cover.

Both gaps cost this build a full test-and-document cycle on a package that could never have deployed, and section 3.1's driver's log has no column for that - a step can be built, tested green and documented while being undeployable, and the tier's ceremony budget assumes the offline gates mean more than they do.
